content.description:
Overall composition
- Full-screen pale-lavender background (#F3F1F6 approximated) with a single centered white card (rounded corners, soft shadow) sitting in the middle of the viewport. The card has a subtle 1px vertical divider between two columns. There is generous whitespace around the card; top-left shows a small circular brand mark, top-right a simple text link “Open Account >”.

Card container
- Background: solid white (#FFFFFF). Corner radius: ~12px. Subtle box-shadow: rgba(16,24,40,0.06) with blur ~24px and offset y ~8px. Thin border or inner stroke subtle (rgba(16,24,40,0.03)). Padding inside card: ~28–32px. Card width ~720–820px on desktop, height ~360–420px.
- Layout: two-column split. Left column (auth form) occupies roughly 60% of card width; right column (referral / promo) ~40%. The columns are separated by a 1px vertical divider color #F0F1F6.

Left column (Log in form)
- Heading: “Log in” — left-aligned, font-weight semibold (600), size ~20px, color #0F1724 (very dark gray). Margin below heading ~16px.
- Email input: single-line text input with light rounded rectangle background (#FAFAFB) or white with border #E7E8EE, border-radius 8px, height ~40px, inner padding 12px. Placeholder/filled text ~14px regular, color #111827. Example value shown (refere.design.team@gmail.com).
- Password input: same style as email; displays obscured characters; right side of input contains an eye icon button (icon color #9CA3AF) to toggle visibility. Space below as small “Forgot password?” link — font-size 13px, color #6B7280 (muted), left-aligned.
- Primary CTA: “Log in” button — rounded (8–10px radius), height ~40px, horizontal padding ~20–24px. Background: vivid indigo/purple blue — approximated gradient or solid #4F46E5 (#5B4BFF is acceptable). Text: white, weight 600, font-size ~14–15px. Button has subtle shadow and hover state: slightly darker shade.
- Secondary action: “Continue with passkey” — a full-width or wide pill-style secondary button beneath primary area, light gray background (#F6F7FA), border 1px solid #ECECF2, icon on left (passkey key icon or shield), text ~14px medium weight, color #374151. Height ~40px, rounded radius 8px. Secondary explanatory text below: small muted copy (~12px, #6B7280) describing passkey option with inline link “Learn how to set it up” underlined or colored (#4F46E5).
- Spacing: Group inputs vertically with 12–16px gap. Section bottom padding ~20px.

Right column (Referral / Share the love)
- Heading: “Share the love” — left/top of the column or aligned to top-left of this column; font-size ~16–18px, weight 600, color #111827. Short paragraph below describing referral terms — small body copy 13–14px, color #6B7280, line-height 18px.
- Referral link pill: a compact input or copyable pill showing a short URL (mercury.com/...), with a small copy icon on the right. Pill background ~#F5F6FA, border-radius 8px, padding 10px, font-size 13px.
- Promo illustration card: centered in column, square / slightly rectangular image with subtle gradient background (lavender→deep purple) and two small CTA outlines “Give $250” and “Get $250” arranged vertically inside the graphic. The illustration uses a soft linear gradient (example: from #EDE7FF to #D6CCFF) with subtle curved line texture. Under illustration a small “View Disclosure” link in muted text (#9CA3AF) sized 12px.
- Column content aligned vertically with consistent spacing between heading, link pill, illustration, and disclosure.

Typography
- Suggested typeface: modern geometric sans (Inter, SF Pro Text, or system sans). Heading weights semibold (600). Body / input text regular (400). Sizes: heading 20px, subheading 16–18px, body / inputs 14px, microcopy 12px. Line-height: headings ~24px, body ~20px.

Colors (approximations)
- Page background: #F3F1F6
- Card background: #FFFFFF
- Primary text: #0F1724 (very dark gray)
- Muted text/copy: #6B7280
- Input border / subtle lines: #E7E8EE or #EEF0F4
- Primary CTA: #4F46E5 to #5B4BFF (gradient acceptable). Text on CTA: #FFFFFF
- Secondary button background: #F6F7FA, border #ECECF2, text #374151
- Divider between columns: #EEF0F4
- Illustration gradient: from #EDE7FF → #D6CCFF and accents in #8B5CF6, #6D28D9

Icons and imagery
- Small circular brand mark at top-left: simple line-mark / logo in dark gray. Top-right “Open Account >” is a text link with subtle chevron icon.
- Eye icon inside password input (toggle). Copy icon next to referral link. Small arrow chevron in “Open Account >”.

States and interactions
- Input states: default border #E7E8EE, focus state with 1–2px outline or glow in primary color #C7D2FE or a 1px border #4F46E5. Disabled state muted (#F3F4F6).
- Button states: default (solid purple), hover (slightly darker), active (pressed inset), disabled (muted gray background, low opacity).
- Copy/clipboard affordance on referral link: clicking copy briefly shows a tooltip/toast “Copied” (0.9–1.8s) — easing: ease-out.

Accessibility notes
- Sufficient contrast on primary CTA and important text. Inputs have labels or placeholders; eye icon has accessible name. Buttons reachable by keyboard; focus outline visible (2px). Copy link provides live region announcement.

Animation notes
- Minimal micro-interactions: button hover 120–160ms ease, input focus highlight 120ms, copy-to-clipboard toast slide/fade-in 200ms ease-out. No heavy motion on main layout.

Overall visual language
- Clean, minimal, modern and friendly. Heavy use of white space and soft pastels/purples for brand accents. Rounded geometry, subtle shadows, and a two-column card that separates authentication actions from a secondary promotional referral block.
content.layout:
Global layout
- Screen: single full-bleed background with a centered card container. The card is the primary focus, horizontally centered with generous side margins.
- Card: 2-column layout divided by a vertical divider. Columns not nested; they are siblings inside the card flex container.

Columns
- Column count: 2 columns (Left: Auth Form, Right: Referral / Promo). Left column width ~60%; right column width ~40% (ratio approx 3:2). 
- Column grouping: Each column contains stacked groups (heading, form controls, CTAs on left; heading, referral link, illustration, disclosure on right). Vertical stacking uses consistent spacing (12–20px gaps) and inner paddings.

Rows and alignment
- The left column uses a vertical flow with rows:
  1) Heading row (Log in) aligned left
  2) Email input row
  3) Password input + forgot link row
  4) Primary CTA row
  5) Secondary CTA (passkey) row + microcopy row
- The right column vertical flow:
  1) Heading + short description
  2) Referral link pill row
  3) Illustration/graphic block (centered inside column)
  4) Disclosure link row

Grid-like structure
- The card behaves like a two-column grid (1 row, 2 columns). Within each column, elements are placed using a vertical single-column stack. Spacing uses an 8px baseline grid with multiples for margins/paddings (8–32px increments).

Breakpoints (responsive behavior - suggested)
- Desktop (>=1024px): two-column card as shown.
- Tablet (640–1024px): columns may stack vertically; promo block below auth form or become horizontally smaller; card width becomes fluid.
- Mobile (<640px): single-column stacked layout: header, email, password, primary CTA, passkey button, then referral block; padding reduced to ~16px, control heights maintained.

Layout keywords
- center-aligned card
- two-column split
- vertical stack in columns
- 3:2 column ratio
- subtle vertical divider
- spacious white space
- rounded corners
- soft shadow
- top navigation link
- copyable referral pill
content.functions:
Specific user actions (micro-level)
- Enter email address into email text field. The input supports typed text, cursor movement, and copy/paste.
- Enter password into password field; toggle visibility by clicking the eye icon that switches between obscured and plain text. The password field may validate length or characters on submit.
- Click “Log in” primary button to submit credentials. On submit, the UI should provide feedback: loading indicator on the button, error messages inline under inputs if invalid, or navigation to the authenticated area on success.
- Click “Forgot password?” link to open a recovery flow (likely a separate modal or route).
- Click “Continue with passkey” to trigger device/native passkey authentication (platform prompt). The button provides explanatory microcopy and a link to learn how to set it up.
- Interact with the referral link: select or click the copy icon to copy the referral URL to clipboard; a small toast or tooltip confirms copy success.
- Click illustration CTAs or “Give $250” / “Get $250” inside the promo visual (if interactive) to view details or start referral actions.
- Click “View Disclosure” to read legal terms — likely opens a modal or navigates to a disclosure document. 
- Click top-right “Open Account >” to navigate to the account creation flow.

Medium-level tasks (workflows)
- Authenticate and gain access: user completes the credentials fields or uses passkey, triggers validation, receives feedback, and is granted access to the account dashboard.
- Recover account: by clicking “Forgot password?” user is guided through a password reset flow (email verification, set new password).
- Use referral: user copies their referral link and shares externally; system tracks referrals and credits rewards when conditions are met.
- Learn about passkey setup: the user follows the informational link to enable passwordless sign-in for future faster authentication.

Higher-level goals (macro-level)
- Primary goal: allow returning users to securely log in to their account with either password or passkey in one central, low-friction interface while presenting promotional referral incentives.
- Secondary goal: surface a referral program and encourage users to copy/share their unique link (visibility of reward and quick-copy affordance increases referrals).
- Tertiary goal: reduce friction for sign-in with passkeys and provide quick access to account creation for new users via the “Open Account” link.

How the UI supports goals
- Clear separation (left column) focuses the user on signing in, while the right column provides contextual marketing without distracting the primary task.
- Large, high-contrast primary CTA for quick recognition; secondary passkey CTA offers alternative secure flows.
- Copyable referral pill and prominent visual reinforce the referral program; explanatory microcopy clarifies requirements (e.g., deposit conditions).

content.description: A clean, minimalist account settings interface with a very light gray-white workspace and subtle dividers, strongly resembling a cloud storage product’s security preferences screen. The overall visual style is sparse, modern, and utility-focused, with a neutral palette dominated by off-white backgrounds and dark neutral text. Main background is #FAFAFA / RGB(250,250,250), side panels and separators use very light gray tints around #F1F1F1 to #E6E6E6, primary body text is near-black #1A1A19 / RGB(26,26,25), secondary labels and muted copy use medium gray tones around #696764 / RGB(105,103,100) and #999897 / RGB(153,152,151). Accent color appears as a warm orange-red #D05E3A / RGB(208,94,58) in the circular user avatar at the top right and small status highlights. The typography is a modern sans-serif system style similar to Inter, Helvetica Neue, or Arial, with a clear hierarchy: page title in larger semibold text, section labels in medium-weight small caps-like tab labels, and supporting descriptions in smaller light-to-regular weight gray text. The top bar includes a large rounded search input with a thin light-gray border, placeholder text “Search,” and a magnifying-glass icon at the left. On the far right, a text button “Invite members” is paired with a small user-add icon, followed by a small circular avatar badge with initials in white on orange-red background. The left sidebar is narrow and icon-driven on the far left, with stacked navigation icons and labels, and a second wider navigation panel showing Home and subitems such as All files, Photos, Shared, File requests, and Deleted files. Sections like Quick access and Starred are displayed with compact spacing and disclosure arrows, plus a small plus icon beside Quick access. The main content area begins with the heading “Personal account,” then a horizontal tab row: General, Security, Notifications, Apps, Branding, Refer a friend, Privacy, Sharing. The active tab “Security” is indicated by darker text and a thin underline. Below, the page is organized into full-width rows separated by fine horizontal rules. Each row has a left-aligned feature title, sometimes followed by a rounded “Recommended” pill in pale blue with blue text, and a short helper sentence beneath in smaller gray text. On the right side of each row are action controls aligned to the far edge: text links such as “Add a recovery email,” “Manage passkeys,” “Change password,” “Show,” and “Start checkup,” styled as dark text links with subtle underline on hover/active behavior implied by link-like appearance. The 2-factor authentication row includes an inline toggle switch on the right in the off state, with a dark circular knob positioned left and a light track, accompanied by the label “Off.” The Recovery email address row includes a right-aligned action link. The Passkeys row shows the action “Manage passkeys” and a small muted count “1 passkey” beneath it. Lower on the screen, a “Web browsers” section contains a bordered table with a light gray header row and columns for Browser, Location, and Most recent activity. One visible entry shows Chrome on Mac OS X, a location in Piscataway, New Jersey, United States, and current session status with a small info icon. Additional security sections continue below, such as Devices, Paper mobile devices, and Mobile contacts, each separated by ample white space and thin dividing lines. The overall spacing is generous, with left-aligned content in a centered main column, subtle card-like table boundaries, and no heavy shadows or decorative imagery, emphasizing clarity and administrative control.
content.layout: Desktop settings layout with a two-panel left navigation and a large content canvas on the right. The far-left rail is a narrow icon column with vertically stacked navigation icons and labels; beside it sits a wider sidebar panel with section title Home, followed by a vertical list of navigation links and a Quick access group. The main workspace occupies the remaining width and is centered with generous margins. At the top of the main area there is a full-width search bar aligned left within the content header, and right-aligned account actions including an invite button and circular user avatar. Below the header, the page title appears above a horizontal tab strip with 8 tabs. The content is arranged as a single-column list of settings rows, each row spanning the main content width and separated by thin horizontal rules. Each row follows a two-zone structure: left zone for title and description, right zone for the action control or status. The browser section introduces a bordered table with a header row and one visible data row, laid out in 3 main columns plus subtle icon/status cell content. Lower sections continue in the same one-column stacked structure. There is no masonry or card grid; the structure is a structured settings form with tab navigation and table-based details.
content.functions: Users can review and manage account security settings from this screen. At the smallest interaction level, they can toggle two-factor authentication on or off, click to add a recovery email, manage passkeys, change password, reveal recovery codes, and start a security checkup. They can also inspect signed-in browser sessions and see device-related account connections. The interface supports careful security maintenance by grouping related actions into distinct rows with explanatory helper text and clear right-aligned actions, so users can understand what each feature does before making changes. At a broader workflow level, a user can harden account security by enabling 2FA, adding recovery methods, updating authentication methods, and reviewing active sessions for suspicious access. The browser table helps them confirm where their account is currently signed in and whether a session is active. Over the larger purpose of the screen, users are able to manage the security posture of their personal account in one place, reducing risk of unauthorized access and providing recovery options if they lose access to email or phone. The page is designed for administrative self-service: it lets the user audit, configure, and verify key security protections without leaving the account settings area.
